policy: The shareable build (repurposing_view.py run --source shareable) embeds a third-party row only when its provenance is listed here as class A. Every other third-party row is represented by an identifier and by counts. An attribution is never removed to make data look distributable: the footer of the output lists the sources actually embedded, and separately the sources that contributed counts or identifiers only. Classes: A attribution (redistribute with credit, only the fields the source's own authors own); B share-alike (never merged into the single page: a separate file with its own licence text and credit line, or counts only); C identifiers and counts only; D local only. Conclusions are those of the licence reconciliation of 2026-10-28 (IT5 P1, catalog/README.md) as corrected by its independent verification of 2026-10-29 (locator_audits/2026-10-29_it5_p1_independent_verification.md): NCI moves to counts-only until its terms are read at NCI; MATRIX is class A for the fields its authors own (names, approval flags) and identifiers-only for the ATC, DrugBank and ChEBI identifiers inside it. IT5 P13 added the claim_source_policy table (every claim source of the catalogue is classified; an unclassified source fails the audit), the card-row attribute rule and the class-B file for ChEMBL. This file implements the mechanism and decides nothing new in law. It is not legal advice.

access_scope_rule: a per-compound access category is embedded only when the catalogue record states it from a class-A scope (openFDA NDC, MATRIX); categories that come from ChEMBL (experimental) or DSLD (supplement) are withheld from individual compounds and survive only as catalogue-wide counts; 'unknown/unverified' is an absence statement, not source content, and is kept

PubMed bibliographic facts.licence: bibliographic facts (PMID, title, journal, year); no abstract and no passage of an article is embedded; article and abstract rights stay with their holders (NLM policy)
PubMed bibliographic facts.attribution: Bibliographic data: PubMed, National Library of Medicine (https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/)
